conflicts.problem: Lesson 5 says plants shift to lactic acid in waterlogged roots and says 'CO₂ produced during aerobic respiration in sukuma wiki leaves' caused the bubbles, while also describing the mandazi phenomenon as the 'anchoring phenomenon' on Mama Wanjiku's counter, which contradicts the anchoring phenomenon (sukuma wiki bubbles, Mwalimu Njoroge's class). Lesson 5 also claims yeast produce 'lactic acid in plant roots'. Plant roots under waterlogging mainly produce ethanol, while Lesson 12 says ethanol and CO2 (or lactate).

Lessons disagree on whether the leaf bubbles are CO2 (Lessons 4, 11: CO2 from respiration, released through stomata and lenticels) or CO2 plus O2 (Lessons 8, 12). Lesson 4 says 'partly CO2' and Lesson 8 says O2 from photosynthesis; Lesson 11 says only CO2. No lesson tested the bubble gas, so the lessons conflict on what the gas is. Also Lesson 11 states bubbles exit through lenticels, though sukuma wiki leaves have no lenticels.

Lesson 10 says groups were 'formed in Lesson 8' and carry out investigations on plant gas exchange (stomatal counts, leaf coating), but Lesson 9 launched anaerobic-respiration projects (yeast, biogas, food fermentation), and Lesson 11 reports presentations on anaerobic investigations. The project content conflicts across Lessons 8–11.
